Why Andover Homes Need Pest Control

Andover sits in a climate sweet spot that unfortunately appeals to more than just the families filling our 5,341 housing units. With an average high of 68°F and average low of 49°F, we experience 36 freeze-thaw cycles annually—and every single one of those cycles drives rodents, spiders, and overwintering pests to seek the warmth of your walls and attic spaces. When temperatures drop between October and April, field mice don't politely wait outside. They're looking for the same comfortable indoor environment your family enjoys.

The median household income of $110,599 reflects a community that's invested in maintaining beautiful properties, from the established homes near Redbud Trail along Main Street and Harrison to the newer developments that have transformed Andover into Butler County's most populated city. But even the best-maintained home is vulnerable when spring arrives. Our 11 inches of annual snowfall might seem modest, but the melt creates moisture conditions perfect for carpenter ants and termites exploring foundation cracks.

Kansas has seen 100 federal disaster declarations in the last ten years—99 of them for severe storms—and Andover knows this reality better than most. Four years ago, a devastating tornado reminded residents that our weather can turn violent. Those same severe weather patterns that bring National Weather Service ICT office alerts to your phone also bring pest pressure. Wind damage creates entry points, storm debris provides harborage, and the standing water that occasionally appears even in our FEMA Flood Zone X classification breeds mosquitoes by the thousands.
